children.name: text
children:
warrants that in the preparation and execution of such design it shall
use the reasonable, skill, care and diligence expected of an
appropriately qualified sub-contractor experienced in carrying out
design work of a similar size, scope and complexity to the SubContract Works and shall ensure that materials or goods selected for
incorporation into the Sub-Contract Works are not deleterious and are
suitable in all respects and that such design will be safe and suitable
for the purposes set out the Sub Contract Documents, including but
not limited to the satisfaction of any performance requirement which
is included in or referred to or implied in the Sub-Contract Documents.
For the purposes of this clause 3.6, 'deleterious' means materials
which are generally accepted or generally suspected in the
construction industry at the relevant time as
3.6.1.1 posing a threat to health and safety of any person;

3.6.1.3 having or possibly having the effect of reducing the normal life
expectancy of the Development or any part of component thereof;

3.6.1.4 do not comply with or are not in accordance with the
recommendations of the Guidance 'Good Practice in the Selection of
Construction Materials 2011' published by the British Council of
Offices and the BRE Digest (or any updated versions of the Guidance
or Digest); or

3.6.1.5 are not in accordance with any relevant British Standard, Code
of Practice, good building practice or techniques where such
Standards, Codes, building practices or techniques exist for the
material concerned.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor is responsible for all necessary fixings and
supports, including but not limited to secondary steelwork and mating
flanges and the like and prior to installation the Sub-Contractor shall
inspect all surfaces to which the Sub-Contract Works shall connect.
Should such inspection reveal any issue whatsoever with any prior
work by others then the Sub-Contractor shall forthwith notify the
Contractor in writing of same. For the avoidance of doubt absence of
such written notice by the Sub-Contractor shall be deemed to be
acceptance by the Sub-Contractor of the suitability of such prior work
and no claims in connection therewith shall be entertained.

The Sub-Contractor shall be deemed to have visited the site and fully
acquainted itself with all aspects of the same. No claims by the SubContractor for lack of knowledge will be entertained.

children.name: text
children:

children.name: text
children:

instructions, drawings, levels or other information which it considers
may be required for the carrying out and completing of the SubContract Works.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall indemnify the Contractor in respect of
losses, costs (including legal costs), expenses, liabilities and/or
damages suffered or incurred by the Contractor by reason of or as a
consequence of any act, omission, default or breach of the SubContract by the Sub-Contractor.

Where drawings, details, design calculations, documents, information
and the like issued pursuant to this clause result in a Variation to the
Sub-Contract Works as defined in the contract preamble then such
Variation shall be valued in accordance with clause 6.2 save that it is
a condition precedent to the Sub-Contractor’s entitlement to any
increase in the Sub-Contract Sum and/or an extension of time as a
result of such Variation that the Sub-Contractor has given written
notice of its intention to claim such increase and/or extension
together with the amount and/or period within 7 days after receipt by
the Sub-Contractor of the said drawings, details, design calculations,
documents, information and the like and has provided the Contractor
with full and satisfactory substantiation of any claimed increase
and/or extension by the earlier of 21 days after receipt by the SubContractor of the said drawings, details, design calculations,
documents, information and the like or such lesser period as may be
required under the Contract.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall on or within a period proximate to the date
when it is reasonably necessary for the Contractor to examine them
and without charge to the Contractor provide to the Contractor (in
agreed format) such drawings, details, specifications, levels, setting
out dimensions, samples and other information which are;

a. reasonably necessary to explain or amplify the Sub-Contract design
or method of working
b. required for approval under the Contract

c. required for the coordination of the Sub-Contractor’s proposals with
those of the Contractor and other contractors working on the site

d. required in order to enable the Sub-Contract Works to be carried
out and completed in accordance with the Sub-Contract;
e. required to comply with any instruction issued under the SubContract;

and the Contractor shall within a reasonable period return one copy of
such drawings, details, specifications, levels, setting out dimensions,
samples and other information to the Sub-Contractor with its
comments and/or the comments of the Contractor’s client or endorse
‘no comment’.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall take account of any comments by the
Contractor and/or the Contractor’s client and shall re-submit until
such time as the drawings, details, specifications, levels, setting out
dimensions, samples and other information is returned by the
Contractor without comment.

No approval or comment or omission to approve or comment on the
part of the Contractor or the Contractor’s client shall be construed as
a Variation nor shall it in any way reduce or limit any duties,
responsibilities, or liabilities of the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
Copyright in all plans, drawings, specifications, designs, details,
reports, schedules, records, calculations and other documents
produced by the Sub-Contractor in connection with the Sub-Contract
Works shall remain vested in the Sub-Contractor but the SubContractor hereby grants and agrees to grant to the Contractor, with
full right to sub-licence to any other party with an interest in the
Works, a non-exclusive, irrevocable royalty free licence to use and
reproduce such drawings, specifications, designs, details, reports,
schedules, records, calculations and other documents for all purposes
relating to the Contract, including construction, completion,
reconstruction, modification, extension, repair, use, maintenance,
letting, sale, renewals, redevelopment, alteration, extension,
reinstatement, marketing and advertisement of the project to which
the Contract Works relate, provided that the Sub-Contractor shall not
be responsible for any use made of such documents by the Contractor
or any other party whatsoever for any purpose which is not permitted
by this clause or for any use for which the documents have not been
prepared. Such licence shall survive any termination of the SubContract.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable and in
sufficient time to allow the Contractor to fulfill its obligations under
the Contract and without charge to the Contractor provide a minimum
of three copies of operation and maintenance manuals, as-built
drawings and all other information required for the purposes of
preparing a Health and Safety file in compliance with the CDM
Regulations in respect of the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall carry out and complete the Sub-Contract
Works within the Period for Completion stated within the Sub-Contract
Order, subject to any extensions to the same as may be granted by
the Contractor in accordance with Clause 5.8.

children.name: text
children:
Without prejudice to clause 5.1 the Sub-Contract Works are to be
carried out and completed by the Sub-Contractor regularly and
diligently and in such order, and at such time or times and in such
manner so as to accord with the progress of the Contract Works and
the works of others and/or as the Contractor may from time to time
direct.

children.name: text
children:
No guarantee is given or implied that the whole of the Sub-Contract
Works may be executed continuously and the Sub-Contractor is
deemed to have allowed in the Sub-Contract Sum for executing the
whole of the Sub-Contract Works in such a manner and sequence as
the Contractor may reasonably require including working either
continuously or in sections or staging the Sub-Contract Works to suit
the progress of other works. The Sub-Contract Sum is deemed to
cover the cost of multiple visits to site as necessary.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor is deemed, prior to the date of this Sub-Contract,
to have examined the Site and ascertained such information and
details concerning the nature risk and condition of the Site including
the subsurface and hydrological condition and the materials
equipment and facilities required to complete the Sub-Contract Works
sufficiently in advance to ensure completion of the Contract Works in
accordance with the programme.

children.name: text
children:
No failure by the Sub-Contractor to identify or foresee any nature
extent risk or condition whether the Sub-Contract Works have been
varied or not shall entitle the Sub-Contractor to any additional
payment under these Conditions.

children.name: text
children:
If requested by the Contractor the Sub-Contractor shall provide prior
to commencement of the Sub-Contract Works (or at any time
hereafter) a method statement which includes a sequence of work
complying with the programme showing how the Sub-Contractor
intends to execute and complete the Sub-Contract Works in
accordance with this Sub-Contract. The Sub-Contractor shall keep the
method statement fully updated and developed throughout the
course of the Sub-Contract Works. The Sub-Contractor accepts that
there is no guarantee that it will be able to carry out works in
accordance with the method statement and its own planned
sequence of work.

children.name: text
children:
If the Contractor considers the Sub-Contractor is failing to proceed
regularly and diligently with the Sub-Contract Works the Contractor
may, at its sole discretion and without prejudice to any other rights
and remedies it may possess, direct the Sub-Contractor to bring to
site additional resources and the Sub-Contractor shall forthwith
comply with this direction entirely at its own cost. If the SubContractor fails to comply with such direction, then the Contractor
may forthwith supplement the Sub-Contractor’s labour with its own
from another source and all the costs of doing so including (but not
limited to) the costs of such labour shall be borne by the SubContractor.

children.name: text
children:
If and whenever it becomes reasonably apparent that the
commencement, progress or completion of the Sub-Contract Works or
any part thereof is being or is likely to be delayed, the Sub-Contractor
shall forthwith (and in any event by the earlier of 7 days of such
occurrence or 2 days prior to the end of such period as may be stated
in the Contract) give written notice to the Contractor of the material
circumstances including the cause or causes of the delay and identify
in such notice any event which in its opinion is grounds for extension
of time.

children.name: text
children:
In respect of each and every ground for extension of time identified in
the notice given in accordance with paragraph 5.8.1 the SubContractor shall, if practicable in such notice or otherwise in writing
by the earlier of 14 days of the service of such notice or 2 days prior
to the end of such period as may be stated in the Contract provide
the Contractor with:
a. full particulars of the event and the causes of the same
b. full particulars of the expected effects thereof

c. the estimated delay (if any) to completion of the Sub-Contract
works resulting therefrom whether or not concurrently with delay
resulting from any other ground for extension of time

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding the foregoing the Sub-Contractor shall at all times use its best endeavors to avoid delay to the Sub-Contract Works and/or mitigate the effects of any event which is likely to cause or does cause.,

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor is delayed in the execution of the Sub-Contract
Works by the occurrence of a Relevant Event as defined in the Main
Contract or by an act, omission or default of the Contractor and such
delayed execution has resulted in critical delay or will result in critical
delay to the completion of the Sub-Contract Works then provided that
the Sub-Contractor has complied with all the requirements in this
clause 5.8 (compliance with which by the Sub-Contractor being a
condition precedent to any entitlement) the Contractor shall grant
such extension of time as the Contractor may in all the circumstances
deem fair and reasonable.

Nothing in this clause 5.8 shall be construed as entitling the SubContractor to any extension of time which may be caused by any act,
omission or default of the Sub-Contractor, its sub-subcontractors,
suppliers, servants or agents, including any instances where the
effect(s) of such cause(s) is concurrent with any other cause(s) of
delay.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall comply with the directions of the Contractor
and carry out such Variations to the Sub-Contract Works as may be
issued in writing by the Contractor in accordance with the SubContract. The Sub-Contractor shall not proceed with any Variations
without first having received the same in writing from the Contractor.

Without prejudice to the above the Sub-Contractor shall comply with
all written instructions issued to him by the Contractor but not
otherwise.

children.name: text
children:
The valuation of Variations (including a Variation which constitutes an
omission of any part or parts of the Sub-Contract Works) shall be
ascertained by the Contractor by reference to any rates or prices
included in the agreed Schedule of Rates for similar or analogous
work. If there are no such rates or prices, or if such rates or prices are
not applicable, then the valuation shall be such as is deemed to be
reasonable by the Contractor in all of the circumstances. The SubContractor shall provide the Contractor with any information,
requested by the Contractor and/or which is otherwise reasonably
necessary, for such valuation.

children.name: text
children:
The valuation of Variations shall only be on a daywork basis where it
is the appropriate basis for valuation and the Sub-Contractor has first
been directed in writing by the Contractor to carry out the Variation
on a daywork basis. The Contractor’s signature on any daywork sheet
will only be taken as verification of the resources used and shall not
be construed as acceptance of any Variation, authority for the
execution of any work or as any evidence whatsoever for additional
entitlement to payment by the Sub-Contractor.

Without prejudice to the above, the Sub-Contractor shall present all
daywork sheets to the Contractor for signature by no later than the
end of the week in which the work is carried out otherwise such
daywork sheets shall in no circumstances be signed or otherwise
entertained. No dayworks, variations or other additional works will be
allowed unless authorised in writing by the Contractor’s Quantity
Surveying Department – For the avoidance of doubt Site
Instructions/daywork sheets issued or signed by the Contractor’s Site
Managers will not be accepted as a basis for the valuing of variations.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contract Sum shall be adjusted to take account of the value
of all Variations, instructed in writing and carried out and completed
by the Sub-Contractor and/or where the Variation constitutes an
omission of part or parts of the Sub-Contract Works. The Sub-Contract
Sum shall not be adjusted for any Variation that was necessitated in
whole or in part by any act, omission, default or breach by the SubContractor.

children.name: text
children:
In the event of an omission of part or parts of the Sub-Contract Works,
the Sub-Contractor confirms that the Contractor may engage others
to undertake such works on whatsoever terms the Contractor
considers appropriate and such omission and reallocation of Works
will not give rise to any actions, loss of profit, claims, rights, demands
and set-offs by the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
Subject to clause 7.2 the Sub-Contractor shall be entitled to its direct
loss and/or expense incurred as a direct result of a Matter as defined
in the Contract and/or a breach of the Sub-Contract by the Contractor
provided that such loss and/or expense shall not exceed the damages
which would otherwise have been recoverable by the Sub-Contractor
at common law in respect of such breach and further provided that
the Sub-Contractor shall take all practicable steps to avoid or reduce
the loss and expense incurred or to be incurred.

children.name: text
children:
It shall be a condition precedent to entitlement under clause 7.1 that
the Sub-Contractor give notice in writing to the Contractor, that it has
been affected by a matter as defined in the Main Contract or that
Contractor is in breach of the terms of the Sub-Contract, within the
timescales set out in the Contract less 3 days or within 14 days of the
date of such breach. Such notice shall expressly state that it is given
pursuant to clause 7.1 and it shall be accompanied by such details
and particulars of the loss and/or expense which the Sub-Contractor
has incurred or expects to incur as a result of the matter or breach
described in the notice.

children.name: text
children:
The amount of any loss and/or expense to which the Sub-Contractor is
entitled under clause 7.1 shall be added to the Sub-Contract Sum.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor’s entitlement to recovery of any loss and/or
expense pursuant to this clause 7 shall be its sole remedy in respect
of loss and/or expense and/or damages arising as a result of a Matter
as defined in the Main Contract or breach of the Sub-Contract by the
Contractor. For the avoidance of doubt the Sub-Contractor shall have
no other entitlement to recover loss and/or expense and/or damages
at common law.

children.name: text
children:
Without prejudice to any other rights and remedies it may possess
the Contractor shall be entitled to deduct and withhold from any
amount(s) otherwise due to the Sub-Contractor under the SubContract any sums including those which the Contractor has suffered
or incurred or anticipates suffering or incurring due to any breach of
or failure by the Sub Contractor to observe the provisions of the SubContract or the provisions of any other contract between the
Contractor and the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
When in the Contractor’s opinion the Sub-Contract Works are
practically complete the Contractor shall, within a reasonable time
thereof issue a written statement to that effect.

Such statement may if appropriate be accompanied by a notification
of defects/outstanding works. The Sub-Contractor shall rectify any
defects and complete any outstanding works in the period(s) stated in
any notification of defects/outstanding work issued by the Contractor

For the avoidance of doubt, no issue of any such statement shall be
construed as bringing to an end the Sub-Contractor’s obligation under
the Sub-Contract which shall remain in full force and effect. Nothing
said or done by the Contractor shall act as any waiver of the SubContractor’s obligations under the Sub-Contract either in whole or in
part and no statement or opinion of the Contractor (other than the
Contractor’s finally adjusted Sub-Contract Sum referred to in clause
10.11) shall serve as conclusive evidence of that on which the
statement or opinion is issued.

children.name: text
children:
It shall be a condition precedent to the occurrence of Practical
Completion of the Sub-Contract Works that:

a. All works required to be completed forming the scope of the SubContract Works have been completed (save at the sole discretion of
the Contractor in respect of any defects or outstanding works, details
of which may be attached to the statement of Practical Completion as
referred to above); and

b. All certificates, warranties, as-built drawings, discharge of all
obligations in respect to Building Control and operating and
maintenance manuals and the like in connection with the SubContract works have been delivered to the Contractor by the SubContractor in a form acceptable to the Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor may whenever it considers it necessary so to do and
whether before or after Practical Completion issue notifications of
defects/outstanding works requiring the rectification of any
outstanding work, defect, shrinkage or other fault which shall appear
before Practical Completion or within the Defects Liability Period and
which is due (but not limited to) to materials or workmanship not
being completed or not being in accordance with the Sub-Contract; to
frost occurring; to the Sub-Contractor’s failure to protect the SubContract Works. All work to be completed or made good as the case
may be, and the Sub-contractor shall within the following periods,
from the date of the said notification, commence complying with the
same at no cost to the Contractor.

·Defects/outstanding work classified by the Contractor as Category 1
and so notified to the Sub-Contractor: within 8 hours

·Defects/outstanding work classified by the Contractor as Category 2
and so notified to the Sub-Contractor: within 7 days

·Defects/outstanding work classified by the Contractor as Category 3
and so notified to the Sub-Contractor: within 28 days

·Defects/outstanding work classified by the Contractor as Category 4
and so notified to the Sub-Contractor: within a reasonable time not
extending later than the end of the Defects Liability Period

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall use its best endeavours to complete any
outstanding work or make good any defect, shrinkage or other fault
which it is required to make good under the Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor is responsible for making any arrangements for
access during the Defects Liability Period and shall ensure that the
Contractor is notified of such arrangements not less than 48 hours in
advance of the time when the Sub-Contractor proposes to carry out
work to make good a defect, or defects, notified by the Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
If for any reason the Sub-Contractor is not able to complete
outstanding work or make good a defect, or defects, within the
requisite period of time for the particular Category of
defect/outstanding work the Sub-Contractor shall forthwith notify the
Contractor in writing and provide in such written notification full
details of the reason(s) why the Sub-Contractor is unable to complete
any particular outstanding work or make good any particular defect or
defects within the requisite period of time. The Sub-Contractor shall
in addition include proposals for any temporary measures which may
be implemented pending completion of the full scope of work
necessary to complete outstanding work or make good any defect or
defects.

Such proposals shall include, but are not limited to, details of any redesign, manufacture and delivery times for both any proposed
temporary measures and work necessary to complete outstanding
work or make good a defect or defects. In addition, the SubContractor shall also provide a programme showing the proposed
date on which all work necessary to complete outstanding work
and/or make good the defect or defects will be completed.{br}

The Contractor reserves the right to recover loss and/or expense,
and/or to charge an appropriate administration fee in respect of time
expended by its management staff as result of the Sub-Contractor
failing to complete outstanding work or make good any defect or
defects within the requisite period of time for the particular Category
of defect/outstanding work.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall notify the Contractor in writing once the
outstanding work has been completed and/or the defect or defects
have been made good giving details of the work which it carried out
and the date(s) when such work was completed together with
relevant details of labour and materials used.

children.name: text
children:
Without prejudice to its other rights and remedies, if the SubContractor shall be in breach of any of its obligations under this
clause 9 and/or otherwise fails to comply with an instruction or
direction of the Contractor, issued under any other clause of the SubContract, the Contractor shall be entitled to employ others to comply
with the same and all damage, loss and/or expense suffered or
incurred by the Contractor in so doing shall be borne by the SubContractor

The term Emergency is defined as and will include but is not limited
to the following;

· any outstanding work and/or defect in the Sub-Contract Works which
materially and immediately affects performance of the Sub-Contract
Works and/or the project and/or the enjoyment or safe occupation of
the same and/or which may immediately affect the health, safety and
wellbeing of the building's owners, occupiers or visitors

children.name: text
children:
In the event of an Emergency (including an out of hours Emergency)
as defined above the Contractor will contact the Sub-Contractor and
the Sub-Contractor will be required to confirm within 1 hour of such
contact that it will attend to the matter.

Should the Sub-Contractor be unable to attend to the Emergency for
any reason and/or in the absence of such confirmation within 1 hour
by the Sub-Contractor, the Contractor shall be entitled to employ
others to attend to the Emergency and all damage, loss and/or
expense suffered or incurred by the Contractor in so doing shall be
borne by the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall be entitled to interim payments at monthly
intervals during the period up to the last working day of the month
following Practical Completion. Each interim payment period shall end
on the last working day of each calendar month or as otherwise
stated in the Sub-Contract Order.

children.name: text
children:
All interim payments shall be subject to the deduction of a retention
amount equivalent to 5% (or such other amount as may be stated in
the Sub-Contract Order).

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall submit a fully detailed gross cumulative
interim application for payment to the Contractor on the fifth working
day prior the end of each interim payment period specifying the sum
that the Sub-Contractor considers to be due up to the end of the
relevant interim payment period (the "Interim Application"). The SubContractor must also specify the basis on which the sum it considers
to be due is calculated and provide full and complete details and
particulars including, but not limited to, measure records, timesheets,
as-built records, delivery tickets, invoices and the like. The valuation
in respect of variations shall be included within the Interim
Application. The Sub-Contractor shall submit in such detail as the
Contractor shall reasonably require full substantiation of the sums
claimed.

children.name: text
children:
The due date for the payment of each interim payment shall be 14
days after the end of the relevant interim payment period. The final
date for payment for each interim payment shall be 15 days after the
due date for that payment.

children.name: text
children:
Not later than five days after the date on which each interim payment
becomes due the Contractor shall give notice to the Sub-Contractor,
“the Payment Notice”, subject to any Pay Less Notice given by the
Contractor under clause 10.6, specifying the sum that the Contractor
considers to have been due at the payment due date and specifying
the basis on which that sum is calculated. If the Contractor does not
issue any such Payment Notice within 5 days of the due date, the
Sub-Contractor may issue its notice in default of the Contractors
Payment Notice “the Default Notice”, specifying the sum that the
Sub-Contractor considers to have been due at the payment due date
and specifying the basis on which that sum is calculated. Should the
Sub-Contractor issue a Default Notice, the final date for its payment
shall be postponed by the same period that the Default Notice is
issued after the due date for payment.

children.name: text
children:
If the Contractor intends to pay the Sub-Contractor less than the sum
stated in the Payment Notice or Default Notice issued in accordance
with clause 10.5 or in accordance with clause 10.13, or in lieu of such
notices the Interim Application under clause 10.3, the Contractor shall
issue a pay less notice (a "Pay Less Notice") specifying in such notice
the sum that the Contractor considers to be due at the date of service
of the notice and also specifying the basis on which that sum is
calculated. The latest date for issue of any Pay Less Notice is one day
prior to the final date for payment.

children.name: text
children:
Upon the issue of any such Pay Less Notice in accordance with clause
10.6 the Contractor’s obligation under Section 111(1) of the Housing
Grants Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 as amended by the
Local Democracy Economic Development and Construction Act 2009
will extend only to payment of the sum stated in the Pay Less Notice.

children.name: text
children:
Within two months of Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract Works
the Sub-Contractor shall submit an account representing the total
value of the work carried out by the Sub-Contractor and, after
deducting the aggregate sum of all amounts paid or due to be paid in
all interim payments, shall identify any balance owing to the SubContractor or Contractor as the case may be (the "Final Account").

children.name: text
children:
The Final Account shall confirm such details and particulars as the
Contractor may reasonably require in order to properly value the SubContract Works and to calculate the amount of the finally adjusted
Sub-Contract Sum.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor fails to submit its Final Account as referred to in
Clause 10.8 within two months of Practical Completion of the SubContract Works, the Contractor may give the Sub-Contractor notice in
writing that it intends to calculate the finally adjusted Sub-Contract
Sum upon the expiry of seven days from the date of the written
notice.

children.name: text
children:
If nothing within the Contractor’s finally adjusted Sub-Contract Sum is
disputed in writing within 14 days of its issue to the Sub-Contractor,
the finally adjusted Sub-Contract Sum as sent by the Contractor to
the Sub-Contractor shall be conclusive in calculating the final balance
amount due between the parties.

children.name: text
children:
Following the making good by the Sub-Contractor of all defects,
shrinkages and other faults in the Sub-Contract Works to the
satisfaction of the Contractor the Sub-Contractor shall be entitled to a
final payment of the balance of the adjusted Sub-Contract Sum or
Final Account, if any, and release of the balance of retention, provided
always that such entitlement shall not arise until a period of thirty six
months (or such other period as may be stated in the Sub Contract)
has elapsed following Practical Completion.

children.name: text
children:
Payment of such amounts shall become due one calendar month from
receipt by the Contractor of the Sub-Contractor's Final Account and of
all accompany documentation and information reasonably required by
the Contractor or if no Final Account is submitted by the SubContractor the date of submission of the Contractor's finally adjusted
Sub-Contract Sum and release of the balance of retention in
accordance with clause 10.20 below, which application shall not be
made until entitlement to such amount has arisen as stated above.
The final date for payment shall be 39 days after the payment
became due.

children.name: text
children:
Within five days of the date on which the final payment becomes due
the Contractor shall give notice to the Sub-Contractor specifying the
sum that the Contractor considers to have been due at the payment
due date and specifying the basis on which that sum is calculated
(the "Final Notified Sum").

children.name: text
children:
If the Contractor intends to pay the Sub-Contractor less than the sum
stated in the Final Notified Sum the Contractor shall give Pay Less
Notice specifying the sum that the Contractor considers to be due at
the date of service of the notice and also specifying the basis on
which that sum is calculated. The latest date for issue of any pay less
notice is one day prior to the final date for payment.

children.name: text
children:
Upon the issue of any such Pay Less Notice in accordance with clause
10.17 the Contractor’s obligation under Section 111(1) of the Housing
Grants Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 as amended by the
Local Democracy Economic Development and Construction Act 2009
will extend only to payment of the sum stated in the Pay Less Notice.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor becomes insolvent, as defined by Section 113 of
the Housing Grants Construction and Regeneration Act 1996, the
Contractor need not pay any sum that has already become due
insofar as it has given a pay less notice; or if the Sub-Contractor has
become insolvent after the last date upon which such notice could
have been given by the Contractor in respect of that sum.

children.name: text
children:
Any entitlement to interest by either Party shall be satisfied by simple
interest at a rate of 4% per annum above the official dealing rate of
the Bank of England current at the date that a payment due under
this Sub-Contract becomes overdue.

children.name: text
children:
All payments by the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor are conditional
on the Contractor receiving payment from the Contractor’s client to
the extent that the Contractor’s client and/or any other person
payment by whom is under the contract (directly or indirectly)
required, is insolvent.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor is a registered person within the meaning of the
current regulation regarding Value Added Tax, he shall inform the
Contractor of his registration number and both the Sub-Contractor
and the Contractor shall carry out their respective obligations under
the Value Added Tax Regulations. The Contractor operates a selfbilling system for Value Added Tax purposes with which the SubContractor shall comply.

children.name: text
children:
Title to any goods or materials forming, or to form, part of the SubContract Works shall pass to the Contractor upon delivery of the
goods and/or materials to site or upon payment thereof, whichever
occurs first. Full responsibility for the protection, safety and security
of the goods and materials shall remain with the Sub-Contractor until
Practical Completion.

children.name: text
children: No payments will be made for unfixed materials on site or off site.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall be liable for and shall indemnify and keep
the Contractor indemnified against all claims, proceedings and costs
in relation to personal injury, death, loss and for damage to property
(including the Sub-Contract Works) and/or economic loss arising out
or in connection with the carrying out of the Sub-Contract Works and
shall indemnify the Contractor against any such liabilities and loss.

children.name: text
children:
Any plant, tools, equipment or other property belonging to or
provided or used by the Sub-Contractor its servants or agents for and
during the execution of the Sub-Contract Works shall be at the sole
risk of the Sub-Contractor and the Sub-Contractor shall indemnify any
keep the Contractor indemnified against any and all claims for loss or
damage to or caused by the same.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall maintain adequate insurance with an insurer
of repute of the type and minimum cover for one event as required by
the Contractor and stated in the Sub-Contract Order for those risks
identified in clause 13.1.

Before commencing the works, the Sub-Contractor shall provide
documentary evidence sufficient to satisfy the Contractor that such
insurance is in place and is being maintained.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor is required to have in force Public Liability
Insurance, Employers Liability Insurance and customary Contractor’s
All Risks insurance in accordance with the requirement of clause 13.6
below and shall, upon request form the Contractor, provide copies of
such insurances to the Contractor together evidence that the relevant
policy remains in force, and where reasonably required, evidence of
the payment of the relevant premium.

children.name: text
children:
Where the Sub-Contract Works involves any design work whatsoever
the Sub-Contractor is required to have in force Professional Indemnity
Insurance extended to indemnify the Contractor against all claims and
proceedings which may be made against the Contractor and all
damages, costs and expense by reason of any errors or omissions in
the Sub-Contractors design, and/or failures to comply with the overall
design and/or infringement of any patent rights or copyrights.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall effect (unless a contrary amount is specified
in the Sub-Contract Order in which case that amount shall prevail):

children.name: text
children:
Public Liability Insurance with a minimum indemnity limit of
£10,000,000 for any one incident and an indemnity to principal’s
clause.

children.name: text
children:
Employers Liability Insurance with a minimum indemnity limit of
£10,000,000 and an indemnity to principal’s clause

children.name: text
children:
Professional Indemnity Insurance with a minimum indemnity limit of
£5,000,000 in respect of any one claim or number of claims arising
out of any one cause providing that such insurance is generally
available at reasonable commercial rates. If such insurance ceases to
be generally available at reasonable commercial rates, or if for any
reason the Sub-Contractor believes that it will be unable to maintain
insurance then without prejudice to any other rights the Contractor
may have the Sub-Contractor shall immediately notify the Contractor

children.name: text
children:
Contractors All Risks Insurance covering loss or damage to the SubContract works and materials on site for incorporation into or for use
in connection with the Sub-Contract Works for their full reinstatement
value save to the extent that the Contractor, the Contractor’s client or
the Employer or any other person takes out and maintains relevant
insurance is contractually obliged to insure the Sub-Contract Works
and such materials. The insured parties shall include the Contractor,
the Contractor’s client and the Employer

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor undertakes, warrants and represents that:

children.name: text
children:
neither the Sub-Contractor nor any of its officers, employees, agents
or subcontractors has:

a. committed an offence under the Modern Slavery Act 2015 (an MSA
Offence); or

b. been notified that it is subject to an investigation relating to an
alleged MSA Offence or prosecution under the Modern Slavery Act
2015; or

children.name: text
children: it shall comply with the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and the Modern Slavery Policy,

children.name: text
text
children:
it shall notify the Contractor immediately in writing if it becomes
aware or has reason to believe that it, or any of its officers,
employees, agents or subcontractors have breached or potentially
breached any of Contractor’s obligations under Clause 14. Such
notice to set out full details of the circumstances concerning the
breach or potential breach of Sub-Contractor’s obligations.

children.name: text
children:
Any breach of Clause 14 by the Sub-Contractor shall be deemed a
material breach of the agreement and shall entitle the Contractor to
terminate the agreement in accordance with Clause 21.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall not assign, delegate, subcontract, transfer,
novate, charge or otherwise dispose of all or any of its rights and
responsibilities under this agreement, nor appoint any sub-contractor,
sub-distributor or sub-agent without the prior written consent of the
Contractor, and subject to compliance with Clause 14.2 and 14.3
below.

children.name: text
children:
Where the Sub-Contractor delegates or sub-contracts any of its duties
or obligations under this agreement pursuant to Clause 14.3 it shall at
all times remain liable to the Contractor for the performance of all of
its duties and obligations under this agreement. The contract that the
Sub-Contractor has with a sub-contractor must

children.name: text
children:
contain substantially the same provisions as those provisions in this
agreement, including an obligation to comply with the Modern Slavery
Act 2015 and the Modern Slavery Policy; and

children.name: text
children:
prohibit the sub-contractor from sub-contracting the services it has
agreed with the Sub-Contractor to provide

children.name: text
children:
If the Customer agrees that the Supplier may subcontract its
obligations, the Supplier shall ensure it has the ability to audit its subcontractor to ensure compliance with the Modern Slavery Policy

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall during the term of this Agreement and for
the period of six years thereafter maintain such records relating to
the Goods and/or Services provided to the Contractor under this
agreement as may be necessary to trace the supply chain of such
Goods and/or Services and to enable the Contractor to determine the
Sub-Contractor's compliance with the Modern Slavery Policy.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall conduct a programme of regular training for
its officers, employees, agents, subcontractors and other members of
its supply chain to ensure compliance with the Modern Slavery Policy.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall keep a record of all training offered and
completed by its officers, employees, agents, subcontractors and
other members of its supply chain to ensure compliance with the
Modern Slavery Policy and shall make a copy of such records
available to the Contractor on request.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall indemnify defend and hold harmless the
Contractor and its directors, officers and employees in full and on
demand from and against any and all liabilities, claims, fines,
demands, damages, losses or expenses (including legal and other
professional adviser’s fees and disbursements), interest and penalties
incurred by them howsoever arising whether wholly or in part
resulting from a breach of the Modern Slavery Policy

children.name: text
children:
(a) it carries on its business in an honest, fair and open way and does
not tolerate practices which could be classed as corrupt or acts of
bribery to obtain an unfair advantage, whether engaged in by the
Contractor, its clients, its sub-contractors or suppliers or others with
whom it does business or, in each case, it’s or their respective officers
or employees;

(b) neither it nor any of its officers and employees have ever been
convicted of any offence that amounts to bribery or corruption for the
purposes of the Bribery Act 2010 (referred to as the "Act") and none
of them has been charged or is currently being investigated for any
such offence;

(c) to the best of its knowledge, information and belief, none of its
clients, its sub-contractors or suppliers or others with whom it does
business have ever been convicted of any offence that amounts to
bribery or corruption for the purposes of the Act, none of them has
been charged or is currently being investigated for any such offence
and none of their respective officers or employees have been so
convicted or charged or are being so investigated;

(d) it has and will at all times maintain in place an effective written
policy for addressing the issues and risks raised by the Act and by the
guidance issued from time to time by the Ministry of Justice (or its
successors) under S.9 of the Act (referred to in this clause 17 as the
"Guidance");

(e) it has and will at all times maintain in place adequate measures to
prevent bribery by those associated with it as set out in S.7(2) of the
Act and as explained in the Guidance; and

(f) it has imposed on those associated with it for the purposes of the
Act requirements no less stringent than those set out in this clause
14.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor undertakes to the Contractor to:
(i) a copy of the policy maintained under clause 15.1(d);

(ii) full written particulars of the adequate measures maintained
under clause 15.1(e);

(iii) reasonable written evidence that it has imposed requirements on
those associated with it as required by clause 15.1(f).

children.name: text
children:
Without prejudice to any other provision of the Sub-Contract the SubContractor shall ensure that it and its sub-contractors and agents are
competent and resourced in health and safety issues. The SubContractor shall comply and shall procure compliance by its subcontractors and agents with all duties and obligations under and
pursuant to Statutory Requirements current at the time the work is
carried out, including but not limited to the Health and Safety at Work
act 1974, the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations
2015 (“CDM Regulations”) and all statutory re-enactments or
modifications thereof, any regulations, rules, orders, codes of practice
made pursuant thereto and any guide lines, recommendations and
health and safety procedures published by such bodies to include bit
not limited to the Health & Safety Executive and the Health and
Safety Commission from time to time.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall comply with such Health & Safety
Management rules and requirements as may be issued from time to
time by the Contractor or any other persons duly authorised by the
Contractor. However, the Sub-contractor shall not be permitted to rely
on those site rules as evidence of its compliance with applicable
requirements. All of the Sub-contractor’s employees, servants and
agents will attend any safety induction required by the Contractor or
the Contractor’s client or the Employer prior to commencing work on
site. Such attendance is deemed to have been allowed for in the SubContract Sum. The Sub-contractor shall report all incidents, accidents
and emergencies to the Contractor immediately and provide all
necessary reports and evidence as may be necessary within 48 hours
of the incident.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall contribute to and comply with any health
and safety plan, which relates to the site. The Sub-contractor must
provide all such information and particulars as are necessary to
complete a health and safety file in respect of the project prior to
Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract works. Materials shall be so
far as possible without risk to health or safety of any person.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall co-operate and coordinate its activities with
the Contractor and with all other contractors employed on the site so
as to enable each to fully comply with Statutory Requirements.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall submit to the Contractor not less than 7
days prior to commencing any work on site:

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor warrants that it is and its sub-subcontractors are
competent to perform its/their duties under and pursuant to the CDM
Regulations in respect of the Sub-Contract Works and that the SubContractor and its sub-subcontractors have allocated, or will allocate,
the resources necessary to perform those duties. The sub-Contractor
undertakes to inform the Contractor immediately in writing if it ceases
to be in a position to comply with those warranties and in any event
to provide such additional information in relation to such competence
and resources as may be requested from time to time by the
Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall keep the Sub-Contract Works clean and tidy
as the work proceeds, and shall regularly dispose of all rubbish and
surplus goods and materials arising from the execution of the SubContract Works by removing the same from the site or to such place
on site as may otherwise be designated in the Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor fails to comply with any obligation imposed by
clause 19.1 the Contractor may have the work of cleaning and
tidying-up carried out by other persons and the Sub-Contractor shall
be liable to pay the Contractor the losses, costs and/or expenses so
incurred.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall not assign, factor, transfer or otherwise deal
with the benefit of the Sub-Contract or any part thereof or any
interest or right therein or thereunder without the prior written
consent of the Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
The Sub-Contractor shall not sub-contract the Sub-Contract Works
and shall not sub-contract any part thereof without the prior written
consent of the Contractor, which consent shall not be unreasonably
withheld or delayed. The giving of consent by the Contractor shall not
in any way relieve the Sub-Contractor of any of its obligations or
liabilities under the Sub-Contract and the Sub-Contractor shall be
liable for the acts, omissions, defaults and breaches of its subcontractors as if they were its own acts, omissions, defaults and
breaches.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor shall always be entitled at any time to assign, transfer
and/or charge this Sub-Contract by way of security to any person
without the consent of the Sub-Contractor, and the Sub-Contractor
agrees to sign or execute all such documents, deeds and/or other
such necessary instruments expediently.

children.name: text
children:
No forbearance, indulgence or relaxation on the part of the Contractor
whether orally or in writing or otherwise by its conduct or any one of
its authorised representatives, including but not limited to interim
payments made under the Sub-Contract, shall in any way act as a
waiver or restrict or diminish the rights of the Contractor under the
Sub-contract or give rise to any contentions that the Contractor is
stopped from relying upon and insisting upon strict adherence by the
Sub-contractor to the terms of the Sub-Contract

children.name: text
children:
Where the Main Contract and/or Sub-Contract requires provision of
any Sub-Contractor collateral warranties, the Sub-Contractor shall
immediately comply with such requirements and shall provide
evidence that such warranties have been disclosed to the SubContractor's professional indemnity insurers.

children.name: text
children:
A person who is not a party to the Sub-Contract has no rights under
the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any term of
the Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children:
Each party acknowledges and agrees that in entering into the SubContract, it does not rely on, and shall have no remedy in respect of
any statement, representation, warranty or understanding (whether
negligently or innocently made) of any person (whether party to the
Sub-Contract or not) other than as expressly set out in the SubContract. Nothing in this clause or elsewhere shall, however, operate
to limit or exclude any liability for fraud including fraudulent
misrepresentation.

children.name: text
children:
To comply with NRMM Regulation (EU)2016/1628 all qualifying dieselpowered Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM), utilised during the
execution of your works is required to comply with the scheme’s
emission requirements.

children.name: text
children:
(a) becomes insolvent within the meaning of Section 113 of the
Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 as amended

(c) is failing to regularly and diligently proceed with the rectification of
work which is not in accordance with the Sub-Contract;

(d) is failing to proceed with the Sub-Contract Works regularly and
diligently;

(e) sub-contracts the whole of the Sub-Contract Works or any part
thereof or assigns, factors, transfers or otherwise deals with the
benefit of the Sub-Contract or any part thereof in breach of clause
19.1;

(f) fails to comply with any of the provisions of clauses 14, 15, 16, 17,
18, 19 and 20;
(g) fails to comply with the provisions of clause 3.5; or
(h) commits any other material breach of the Sub-Contract;

then in any such event and provided that in respect of paragraph (c)
and (d), the Contractor has given 7 days prior written notice requiring
the Sub-Contractor to proceed regularly and diligently, then without
prejudice to any other rights or remedies, the Contractor may by
written notice to the Sub-Contractor determine the Sub-Contractor’s
employment under the Sub-Contract with immediate effect.

children.name: text
children:
Notwithstanding any other provision of the Sub-Contract, where the
Sub-Contractor’s employment under the Sub-Contract is determined
pursuant to this clause 21.1 the Contractor shall not be liable to pay
any further sums to the Sub-Contractor (whether under clause 10 or
otherwise) until completion of the Sub-Contract Works and the losses,
costs and expenses incurred by the Contractor in completing the SubContract Works have been ascertained. Such losses costs and
expenses shall be payable by the Sub-Contractor to the Contractor
within 5 days of notification of the same and within 30 days of such
notification the Sub-Contractor shall be entitled to make one final
application for payment in accordance with clause 10.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor may in lieu of giving a notice of determination under
clause 21.1 take part only of the Sub-Contract Works out of the hands
of the Sub-Contractor by giving notice under this clause 21.3
specifying the relevant part and the Contractor may itself or by a
third party execute such part and in such event the Sub-Contractor
shall pay to the Contractor the reasonable additional costs and
expenses incurred by the Contractor as a consequence thereof. The
Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to payment of any other costs,
expenses, damages or losses arising from such termination including
but not limited to any loss of profit, expectation, overheads or
otherwise.

children.name: text
children:
The Contractor may at any time serve notice on the Sub-Contractor
forthwith terminating the employment of the Sub-Contractor. As soon
as reasonably practicable after termination in accordance with this
clause 21.4 and the Sub-Contractor's compliance with 21.6,, the
Contractor shall ascertain the total amount properly due to the SubContractor up to the date of termination which shall include the SubContractor's reasonable costs properly incurred in complying with
clause 21.6 and the final date for payment of such amount to the SubContractor shall be no later than 1 month from the date of service of
such notice. The Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to payment of
any other costs, expenses, damages or losses arising from such
termination including but not limited to any loss of profit, expectation,
overheads or otherwise.

children.name: text
children:
The determination of this Contract is without prejudice to the rights
obligations and liabilities of either party accrued prior to termination.

children.name: text
children:
Upon any termination of the Sub-Contractor's employment under
clauses 21.1 or 21.4 the Sub-Contractor shall immediately:
(b) deliver up to the Contractor all Sub-Contract Documents;

(c) deliver up any plant materials and other work and goods, whether
or not the Sub-Contractor has received payment; and
(d) subject to clauses 21.7 and 21.8, leave the site.

children.name: text
children:
Upon termination the Sub-Contractor shall immediately protect and
secure the Sub-Contract Works and shall immediately then leave the
site and shall deliver to the Contractor 3 no. copies of all designs,
drawings, details, documents and information then prepared by or on
behalf of the Sub-Contractor for the Sub-Contract Works in respect of
which the Contractor shall retain licence to copy, use and/or
reproduce for any purpose and may assign or grant licences under
the licence without the consent of the Sub-Contractor. In the event of
a termination under clause 21.1, the Sub-Contractor shall not The
Employer’s Agent any of its equipment, materials or property from
the Site until completion of the Contract Works and/or shall do so
forthwith upon the direction of the Contractor

children.name: text
children:
For the purpose of completion of the Sub-Contract Works following
termination pursuant to clause 21.1, the Contractor shall have the
free use of the Sub-Contractor's equipment, materials and property
on the Site without responsibility to the Sub-Contractor for fair wear
and tear thereof and shall be entitled to use any materials or goods or
fabricated work at the Site or the Sub-Contractor's workshop or other
premises which have been bought or fabricated for the purpose of the
Sub-Contract. The Sub-Contractor shall without charge and within 10
calendar days of termination, assign the benefits of any agreement
for the supply of such equipment, materials and property to the
Contractor.

children.name: text
children:
If any dispute arises under this Sub-Contract then either the SubContractor or the Contractor may at any time issue a notice to the
other referring such dispute for the decision of an adjudicator, to be
nominated by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors. The
provisions of Part 1 of the Schedule to the Scheme for Construction
Contracts (England and Wales) Regulations 1998 shall apply to any
dispute referred under this clause.

children.name: text
children:
If the Sub-Contractor becomes aware of any inadequacy in or
discrepancy between any of the Sub-Contract and/or Contract
documents, it shall immediately give notice with appropriate details
to the Contractor, who shall issue instructions in that regard. The
Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to any addition to the SubContract sum and/or any other costs, losses and / or expenses arising,
whether directly or indirectly, as a result of such matters.

children.name: text
children:
This agreement shall be governed and construed in accordance with
the laws of England and Wales and shall be subject to the jurisdiction
of the English Courts.
